knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.6.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. For an iid sample with population mean μ and variance σ², which statement about X̄ and S² is correct?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The sample mean is unbiased with variance σ²/n, and the usual S² is unbiased for population variance.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Confusing population variance, variance of the sample mean, and the target of S².

choices.label: E[X̄]=μ, Var(X̄)=σ²/n, and for the usual denominator n-1 sample variance, E[S²]=σ².
E[X̄]=μ/n because averaging divides the expected value by n.
Var(X̄)=σ² because averaging independent observations does not reduce variance.
E[S²]=σ²/n because sample variance estimates the variance of X̄ rather than the population variance.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.6.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly summarises the distribution-free moment results for X̄ and unbiased S²?
knowledge_checks.body: Identify what the moment identities do and do not establish.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Means and variances do not by themselves determine exact sampling distributions.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: State the three moment identities; do not infer exact Normal or t laws from them alone.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating unbiasedness and variance formulas as sufficient for exact distributional results.

choices.label: E[X̄]=μ, Var(X̄)=σ²/n, and E[S²]=σ². These moment results alone do not establish exact Normal, chi-square, or t distribution laws.
Var(X̄)=σ²/n proves X̄ is exactly Normal for every parent population and every n.
E[S²]=σ² proves (X̄-μ)/(S/√n) is t distributed without any population assumptions.
E[X̄]=μ means X̄ equals μ in every sample, so sampling variability is zero.
